1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(starwars)
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = eye_color)) + geom_bar()
```

3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc. 
```{r}
unique(starwars$eye_color)

eye_color_fill <- c(
  "blue" = "#1569C7", 
  "yellow" = "#FFFF00",        
  "red" = "#D94218",           
  "brown" = "#A35E35",         
  "blue-gray" = "#6A89A7",     
  "black" = "#000000",         
  "orange" = "orange",
  "hazel" =  "#8E7618",       
  "pink" = "#F4C0D0",        
  "unknown" = "gray",       
  "red, blue" = "#9E1B1B",     
  "gold" = "#E6B51E",         
  "green, yellow" = "#ADFF2F", 
  "white" = "#F8F5FA", 
  "dark" = "#9e6b4a"
)

ggplot(starwars, aes(y = eye_color, fill = eye_color)) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  theme_apa(remove.x.gridlines = FALSE, legend.pos = "none") + 
  labs(y = "Eye Color", x = "Frequency") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = eye_color_fill) 
```
I tried to match the bar color to the eye color by looking up hex codes for characters. I used unique() to get all the possible eye colors, then put them in a vector before assigning hex codes.
